extracted.intended_audience: readers of Carlyle / educated general readers and literary critics
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial commentary and excerpted passages from Carlyle's Sartor Resartus, focusing on the 'Philosophy of Clothes', Church-Clothes, symbols, vocation, and moral exhortations; aimed at guiding readers through Teufelsdrockh's ideas and indicating how one should interpret them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Everlasting Yea — love God over Pleasure
rubrics_metrics.description: Life rooting out the deep-seated chronic Disease, and triumphs over Death... Love not Pleasure; love God. This is the EVERLASTING YEA, wherein all contradiction is solved: wherein whoso walks and works, it is well with him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as an ultimate ethical orientation: prefer devotion to God rather than pursuit of pleasure; the 'Everlasting Yea' resolves contradiction and is the marker of a well-lived life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worship of Sorrow as an existing phenomenon
rubrics_metrics.description: The '_Worship of Sorrow_'... the Temple thereof, founded some eighteen centuries ago, now lies in ruins... nevertheless, venture forward; in a low crypt... the Altar still there, and its sacred Lamp perennially burning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat certain austere or sorrow-embracing religious impulses as genuine, long-lived spiritual phenomena; recognize their ruins but also their persistent inward presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of Partial Inspiration vs Plenary Inspiration
rubrics_metrics.description: 'try rather to get a little even Partial Inspiration, each of you for himself. One BIBLE I know, of whose Plenary Inspiration doubt is not so much as possible; nay with my own eyes I saw the God's-Hand writing it: thereof all other Bibles are but Leaves.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical spiritual advice: seek attainable, personal (partial) inspiration rather than disputing claims of universal/plenary inspiration; acknowledge a special, unquestioned text but emphasize individual experience of inspiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do the duty nearest thee (priority of proximate obligation)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Do the Duty which lies nearest thee,' which thou knowest to be a Duty! Thy second Duty will already have become clearer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral rule for action and vocation: focus first on the immediate, known duty; action clarifies further obligations. Presented as invaluable, experience-tested counsel for those groping in uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conviction must convert into Conduct (action over speculation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conviction, were it never so excellent, is worthless till it convert itself into Conduct. Nay properly Conviction is not possible till then; ... 'Doubt of any sort cannot be removed except by Action.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for evaluating sincerity or intellectual resolves: assess convictions by whether they produce concrete actions; use action as the test and remedy for doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find and work your Ideal in the Actual (internal vocation criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ideal is in thyself, the impediment too is in thyself: thy Condition is but the stuff thou art to shape that same Ideal out of: what matters whether such stuff be of this sort or that, so the Form thou give it be heroic, be poetic?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical criterion for vocation and creativity: do not wait for an external 'ideal' situation — enact the Ideal within current conditions by shaping available material; the true test of calling is productive work in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Tools and the Pen as primary creative instrument
rubrics_metrics.description: Tools? Hast thou not a Brain, furnished... and three fingers to hold a Pen withal? Never since Aaron's Rod went out of practice... greater than all recorded miracles have been performed by Pens. The WORD is well said to be omnipotent in this world; man, thereby divine, can create as by a Fiat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for creative agency: writing (the Pen, the Word) is emphasized as a chief instrument for shaping the world; immediate exhortation to 'produce' — even small products are valuable.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Man is the spirit he worked in — prioritize spirit over factual biography
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Wilt thou know a Man, above all a Mankind, by stringing together bead-rolls of what thou namest Facts? The Man is the spirit he worked in; not what he did, but what he became.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation rule for biography and interpretation: when judging a life or history, give primacy to the inner spirit and development rather than a mere catalogue of external facts; facts are 'Hierograms' needing keys of interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: What counts as a remarkable incident in modern history
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Perhaps the most remarkable incident in Modern History ... is George Fox's making to himself a suit of Leather.' The first outflashing of man's Freewill to light is the true grandeur of history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reframe historical significance: acts expressing inner freedom, spiritual self-determination, or the turning of daily labour into religious/ethical protest (as Fox's leather suit) can be more historically momentous than battles or political events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Church-Clothes defined and their social importance
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Church-Clothes ... the Forms, the Vestures, under which men have at various periods embodied and represented for themselves the Religious Principle... These are unspeakably the most important of all the vestures and garnitures of Human Existence.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for assessing religion/society: examine the outward forms (rituals, institutions, vestures) through which the religious principle is embodied — they are foundational to social life and to the existence of society itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of Churches (three predicaments)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'every conceivable Society... may well be figured as properly and wholly a Church, in one or other of these three predicaments: an audibly preaching and prophesying Church, which is the best; second, a Church that struggles to preach and prophesy, but cannot as yet; and third and worst, a Church gone dumb with old age, or which only mumbles delirium prior to dissolution.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytic rubric for diagnosing a Church/Society: prefer those actively preaching/prophesying (vital), tolerate those striving (incipient), and condemn those that are inert or merely ceremonial (decayed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signs of hollow Church-Clothes (masks vs living vestures)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'many of them have become mere hollow Shapes, or Masks, under which no living Figure or Spirit any longer dwells; but only spiders and unclean beetles, in horrid accumulation, drive their trade; and the mask still glares on you with its glass eyes...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for judging institutional vitality: identify whether outward forms are alive (embodied spirit) or hollow masks inhabited by corruption; hollow forms indicate societal/spiritual decay and eventual disuse or destruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silence and secrecy as productive conditions for symbols and creation
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The benignant efficacies of Concealment ... SILENCE and SECRECY! Altars might still be raised to them ... Silence is the element in which great things fashion themselves together; that at length they may emerge, full-formed and majestic, into the daylight of Life.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guideline for symbolic/creative practice: avoid premature publicity or babbling about projects—concealment and silence allow complex, great ideas to form before being revealed; creators and leaders should cultivate reticence.
